description: Separate the runner config channel so cleanupPolicy no longer piggybacks on work dispatch: add GET /api/runner/{id}/config on the server, then switch the runner to fetch policy from it on each cleanup-loop tick and remove CleanupPolicy from WorkDispatchResponse on both ends atomically.

tasks.title: Add dedicated GET /api/runner/{id}/config endpoint on the server
tasks.description: Add `group.MapGet("/config", ...)` inside the existing `/api/runner/{runnerId}` route group in RunnerRoutes.cs, returning a new `public record RunnerConfigResponse(CleanupPolicyDto? CleanupPolicy)`. The handler injects `IOptions<CleanupPolicyOptions>` (same binding `/poll` uses) and projects it via the existing `ToCleanupPolicyDto`, returning 200 OK unconditionally — including when the system is idle and when the policy is fully unconfigured. This is purely additive: `/poll` and `WorkDispatchResponse.CleanupPolicy` are untouched in this task.
acceptanceCriteria: `GET /api/runner/{runnerId}/config` returns `200 OK` with a `RunnerConfigResponse { cleanupPolicy }` JSON body.
Endpoint returns 200 with a body even when the system is idle (i.e. when `POST /api/runner/{runnerId}/poll` would return 204); policy availability is never gated by work presence.
Configured `RetentionDays` / `StorageBudgetBytes` / `StorageTargetWatermarkBytes` are projected into the response via the existing `ToCleanupPolicyDto` mapping.
Unconfigured or non-positive policy fields are emitted as `null`, preserving the 'null means unlimited/disabled' contract.
A fully-unconfigured `CleanupPolicyOptions` still yields `200 OK` with all-null `cleanupPolicy` fields (no body omission, no error).
Request is a plain GET with no request body and no ETag / If-None-Match / version negotiation.
The `cleanupPolicy` JSON shape is identical to the existing `CleanupPolicyDto` (runner parses with its existing `CleanupPolicy` TS type without modification).
`/poll` behavior is unchanged in this task: it still returns 204 with no body when idle and still serializes `WorkDispatchResponse.CleanupPolicy` when work is dispatchable (removal is T-002).

Server spec (extending `RunnerCleanupPolicyAndStatusApiSpecs.cs` or a new spec file) covers: configured-values projection, null-sentinel emission, fully-unconfigured policy, idle-system 200-with-body, and plain-GET-no-body — all via the test client / WebApplicationFactory with no real HTTP.
`npm test` (server) passes; no new external dependencies, DB access, or grain calls are introduced.
tasks.output: packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Api/RunnerRoutes.cs (new MapGet "/config" route + RunnerConfigResponse record); updated/added server spec file.
tasks.notes: Design D1 + D5. The `RunnerConfigResponse` wrapper record (rather than returning `CleanupPolicyDto` bare) is deliberate so future runner-facing config fields can be added additively. Route placement reuses the existing route group so whatever auth/gate applies to `/poll` applies to `/config` — no new auth surface.

tasks.title: Switch runner to fetch config on each cleanup tick and remove CleanupPolicy from WorkDispatchResponse on both ends
tasks.description: Atomically (per design D2 + migration plan step 3) swap the runner to the new config channel and remove the legacy dispatch-carried policy: (a) Runner — add `ServerConnection.fetchConfig(signal): Promise<CleanupPolicy | null>` performing `GET /api/runner/{runnerId}/config`; change `host.ts:runCleanupOnce` to `await this.connection.fetchConfig(signal)` and pass the result to `cleanupLoop.runOnce`; delete `lastCleanupPolicy` and `getLastCleanupPolicy()` from `connection.ts`; remove the `this.lastCleanupPolicy = dispatch.cleanupPolicy ?? null` line from `poll()`; remove `cleanupPolicy` from the runner `WorkDispatchResponse` TS type. (b) Server — remove the `CleanupPolicy` parameter from the `WorkDispatchResponse` record and the `CleanupPolicy: ToCleanupPolicyDto(...)` assignment in the `/poll` handler. `poll`'s work-dispatch semantics (204-when-idle, 200+work-envelope-when-dispatchable) are otherwise unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: `ServerConnection.fetchConfig(signal)` performs `GET /api/runner/{runnerId}/config` and returns the `cleanupPolicy` from the parsed body (or null when absent).
`runCleanupOnce` calls `fetchConfig` on every cleanup-loop tick and passes the result into `cleanupLoop.runOnce`; no policy is read from any dispatch-cached field.
Each cleanup-loop tick issues its own GET; the runner performs no ETag / If-None-Match / version-based conditional fetch and does not cache policy between ticks.
`lastCleanupPolicy` field and `getLastCleanupPolicy()` accessor no longer exist on `ServerConnection`; `poll()` no longer reads or stores `dispatch.cleanupPolicy`.
Server's `WorkDispatchResponse` record no longer has a `CleanupPolicy` parameter; the `/poll` handler no longer assigns `CleanupPolicy = ToCleanupPolicyDto(...)`.
Runner's `WorkDispatchResponse` TS type no longer has a `cleanupPolicy` property.

Idle-system behavior: when `poll` is continuously returning 204 and `/config` returns a policy with at least one enabled strategy, the next cleanup-loop tick fetches config, obtains the non-null policy, and runs eviction — cleanup is NOT skipped due to absence of work dispatches.

Idle-system with fully-unconfigured policy: `/config` returns all-null fields, the runner observes no eviction strategy is enabled, and removes nothing (preserving the 'null means do not evict' contract).

`/poll` work-dispatch semantics are otherwise unchanged: no-work still returns 204 No Content with no body; dispatchable work still returns 200 OK with the full work envelope (only `cleanupPolicy` is absent).

`fetchConfig` failure (non-2xx / network error) is best-effort per design D4: it throws, the existing `runCleanupOnce` try/catch logs and skips this tick; no stale fallback cache is kept; the next tick retries.

The three runner host test mocks (`runner-host.spec.ts`, `runner-host-task-log.spec.ts`, `runner-host-convergence.spec.ts`) are updated from `getLastCleanupPolicy = () => null` to `fetchConfig = async () => null` (or a configured policy where the spec needs it).
Server spec asserts `/poll` dispatch body no longer contains a `cleanupPolicy` property; existing poll/dispatch specs updated to drop any `cleanupPolicy` expectation.
Runner spec covers the idle-system cleanup scenario (poll → 204, `/config` → policy, eviction runs) using a fake connection — no real HTTP, no real time.
`npm run typecheck` and `npm run test:run` pass for both `packages/runner` and `packages/web`; `npm test` (server) passes.
tasks.output: packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Api/RunnerRoutes.cs (WorkDispatchResponse.CleanupPolicy removed + /poll assignment removed); packages/runner/src/server/connection.ts (fetchConfig added; lastCleanupPolicy/getLastCleanupPolicy removed); packages/runner/src/runtime/host.ts (runCleanupOnce uses fetchConfig); packages/runner/src/core/types.ts (RunnerConfigResponse added; WorkDispatchResponse.cleanupPolicy removed); updated server + runner specs.
tasks.notes: Design D2 + D3 + D4. Per migration plan, server and runner ship as a managed pair via `mo update server` then `mo update runner`; no cross-version compatibility shim is required, so the field is removed outright rather than carried as a duplicate. Reuse the caller's AbortSignal for `fetchConfig` (matches existing poll/report/workflowRunsStatus helpers in connection.ts) — confirm the cleanup-loop tick signal stays valid for the fetch duration. Deploy/rollback guidance: land server-side removal and runner change atomically; partial rollback (new runner + old server) yields 404s on `/config`, logged and skipped per D4.
